findings.description: The synchronous copy receives the previous thread-local statistics dictionary instead of the wrapper's statistics dictionary. The first invocation therefore leaves the public statistics empty.
findings.rationale: On the first call to a decorated function, wrapped_f.statistics and self._local.statistics are separate dictionaries. Assigning the latter to copy._local.statistics makes retry execution update that separate dictionary, while the public dictionary cleared at line 377 remains empty. Users inspecting statistics after the call, including through an additional decorator, receive no statistics.

findings.description: Overlapping invocations now share a mutable statistics dictionary, so their retry statistics interfere with each other.
findings.rationale: If two overlapping calls to the same async decorated function each fail once and then succeed, both retry copies update the same dictionary. Each call's initialization resets it and each retry increments its attempt count, allowing the final statistics to report three attempts although each call took only two. Previously, each invocation had its own statistics dictionary, keeping the exposed invocation's counts isolated.
